title: Real-world outcomes of first-line gemcitabine-platinum plus an immune checkpoint inhibitor and subsequent treatment with matched targeted therapy in biliary tract cancer.
abstract: Gemcitabine plus platinum combined with an immune checkpoint inhibitor (GP-ICI) is standard first-line therapy for advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC); however, tumor-site distribution, molecular epidemiology, and postprogression treatment access vary globally. We compared real-world outcomes and postprogression treatment patterns between US and South Korean tertiary centers. Patients with advanced BTC receiving first-line GP-ICI at MD Anderson Cancer Center (MDACC) or Asan Medical Center (AMC) between 2021 and 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Outcomes included objective response rate (ORR), progression-free survival (PFS), overall survival (OS), and postprogression survival (PPS). Molecular profiling and treatment patterns were evaluated. Among 375 patients (MDACC, n = 121; AMC, n = 254), intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma was observed at a higher proportion at MDACC (71.9% versus 42.1%), whereas extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma was more common at AMC (10.7% versus 41.7%). ORR (21.5% versus 15.7%), median PFS (6.6 versus 7.2 months), and median OS (19.5 versus 14.9 months) were comparable. Median PPS was significantly longer at MDACC (13.1 versus 5.8 months; P = 0.002). IDH1 mutations and FGFR2 fusions were more common at MDACC, whereas HER2 alterations were more frequent at AMC. Among patients with actionable alterations, matched targeted therapy was administered more frequently at MDACC (75.8% versus 12.8%; P < 0.001) and was associated with significantly longer PPS [hazard ratio (HR) 0.15, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.06-0.41, P < 0.001] and a trend toward longer OS (HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.26-1.10, P = 0.089). Real-world GP-ICI outcomes were comparable between US and South Korean cohorts. The differences in molecular profiling, matched targeted therapy utilization, and postprogression outcomes underscore the need for broader molecular profiling and improved targeted therapy access in advanced BTC.

title: Expansion of KPC-3-producing
abstract: Carbapenemase-producing (CP) Klebsiella pneumoniae are a major public health concern in Portugal, where the population has been dominated by KPC-3-producing ST147-KL64. Following preliminary detection of an unexpectedly high proportion of ST15-KL19 infections after the COVID-19 pandemic, we investigated the recent expansion and clinical relevance of this sublineage. All CP K. pneumoniae isolates recovered from hospitalized patients between 2022 and 2023 (n = 267) were characterized by antibiotic susceptibility testing and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, wzi sequencing and multi-locus sequence typing. Representative ST15-KL19 isolates from a baseline (2019-2021) and the recent expansion (2022-2023) periods were selected for whole-genome sequencing and compared with publicly available global genomes to assess phylogenetic relatedness, temporal structure, and potential links to non-human reservoirs. ST15-KL19 emerged as one of the most frequent CP K. pneumoniae sublineages, increasing from 23% to 35% and replacing ST147-KL64 over time. Genomic analyses identified two temporally distinct ST15-KL19 variants. Isolates from the recent expansion period (2022-2023) acquired bla CTX-M-15 and other plasmid-mediated aminoglycoside resistance determinants, concurrently with an IncR plasmid replicon. Phylogenomic analyses revealed that both variants were already circulating in the region before 2019. Together with the high colonization rates at admission (64%), our data suggest repeated introductions from external sources rather than in-hospital evolution. Global comparisons supported regional and intercontinental dissemination from a common ancestor, though a direct foodborne origin could not be established. This study documents the recent expansion of a previously minor CP K. pneumoniae sublineage, highlighting how shifts in healthcare ecology can favor adaptive variants or repeated introductions. Continuous molecular surveillance is essential to detect such emerging lineages early and to inform infection control and antimicrobial stewardship strategies.

title: Design and evaluation of probe-capture sequencing for clinical
abstract: Characterizing the molecular epidemiology of Neisseria gonorrhoeae is essential for understanding disease burden, elucidating transmission dynamics, and informing clinical decision-making and public health interventions. Given that routine, culture-independent diagnostics rapidly and sensitively detect this difficult-to-cultivate pathogen, aligning genomic surveillance with these workflows is necessary to understand its epidemiology and evolutionary dynamics. To address this challenge, we investigated the utility of probe-capture sequencing to selectively enrich for pathogen-specific DNA during next-generation sequencing. Custom biotinylated oligonucleotide baits were designed using genetic information from publicly available genomes hosted on Pathogenwatch. Of the 32,574 assemblies, 2,877 representative genomes were selected to inform probe generation using core genome amino acid distance clustering and representation of unique resistance-associated genotypes and predicted resistance phenotypes. The resulting probe set provided generous coverage of the reference genome, N. gonorrhoeae FA 1090, with 94.6% nucleotide coverage and 99.3% of annotated genes covered by at least one probe. Piloting this technology on 12 clinical urine specimens with variable relative pathogen abundances revealed that probe-capture sequencing substantially increased the relative abundance of N. gonorrhoeae sequence reads from a complex sample (fold-change range, 226 - 2046), enabling considerable genome coverage, the construction of high-quality genome assemblies, and the detection of resistance-associated genotypes. These findings demonstrate that probe-capture sequencing is a viable method for enriching N. gonorrhoeae genetic material from clinical samples, enabling culture-independent genomic investigations into the epidemiology of hard-to-culture pathogens and providing actionable insights to inform clinical and public health interventions. Understanding the molecular epidemiology of bacterial pathogens can illuminate population diversity, transmission dynamics, and genotypes associated with bacterial traits and clinical outcomes. Difficulties in cultivation hinder our ability to understand the epidemiology of Neisseria gonorrhoeae . Aligning genomic surveillance methodologies with existing clinical diagnostic modalities is essential to guiding the implementation of innovative genomic surveillance. In this paper, we used representative public genome assemblies to design custom biotinylated oligonucleotide baits to successfully increase pathogen-specific DNA yield from complex clinical urine specimens during next-generation sequencing. Probe-capture sequencing markedly improved detection of pathogen-specific genetic material from clinical specimens, enabling construction of high-quality genome assemblies and detection of resistance-associated genotypes. Collectively, we demonstrate that probe-capture sequencing is a viable method for sequencing hard-to-culture pathogens from clinical specimens, highlighting how this technology could strengthen genomic investigations into the epidemiology of these pathogens and provide actionable insights to inform clinical decision-making and public health interventions.

title: Sequence-structured fitness landscapes predict influenza evolution.
abstract: Seasonal influenza viruses continually evolve to evade host immunity. Vaccines must be regularly updated to protect against new circulating strains, motivating efforts to forecast viral evolution. Recent experimental and computational methods have made progress on this problem, but learning the fitness landscape driving viral evolution remains challenging because genomic surveillance samples only a small fraction of the possible sequence space. Here, we developed a generative framework that shares information across genetically related variants, inferring effective mutation-level contributions to viral fitness from temporal sequence data. Applied to hemagglutinin and neuraminidase from A/H3N2 and A/H1N1 viruses, the inferred fitness landscapes recovers known determinants of antigenicity and reveals convergent spatial organization across subtypes consistent with common antibody-mediated selection. Forward simulations from these landscapes predicted both the fixation or loss of circulating mutations and the future composition of viral populations, outperforming models based on neutral evolution or multinomial-logistic growth. Collectively, our results show that interpretable representations of pathogen fitness landscapes can reveal biologically important features and improve prospective evolutionary forecasting.

title: Risk factors and molecular epidemiology of ST2-type carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii carrying bla
abstract: The emergence and spread of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii (CRAB, A. baumannii) has raised significant concerns and challenges globally. This study analyzes the risk factors, distribution of antibiotic resistance genes, and virulence genes associated with CRAB infections, and explores the molecular epidemiological characteristics of CRAB. The findings provide scientific evidence for the development of prevention and treatment strategies for CRAB. A total of 100 patients diagnosed with A. baumannii(AB) infection through culture and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were included in the study. These patients were classified into the CRAB group and the carbapenem-sensitive A. baumannii (CSAB) group based on their susceptibility to carbapenem antibiotics. Univariate analysis was used to screen for factors associated with CRAB infection, and significant variables were included in a multivariate logistic regression analysis. Additionally, five CRAB strains carrying both blaOXA-51-like and blaOXA-23-like genes were randomly selected for multilocus sequence typing (MLST) and whole-genome sequencing. The analysis included the identification of antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs), virulence factor genes, pathogen-host interaction annotations from the Pathogen Host Interactions Database, and functional annotations through Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG). Significant differences were observed between the CRAB group and the CSAB group in terms of length of hospital stay (P = 0.022, OR = 1.068), ICU admission rate (P = 0.019, OR = 8.032), prior carbapenem use (P = 0.028, OR = 4.445), and mechanical ventilation use (P = 0.044, OR = 7.226). In vitro antimicrobial susceptibility testing showed that all CRAB strains were resistant to ceftriaxone, ceftazidime, and ciprofloxacin, with some strains showing resistance to levofloxacin (87.5%) and doxycycline (93.8%), but remaining sensitive to tigecycline and polymyxin B. Through multiplex PCR analysis, we tested 48CRAB strains (carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii). The results revealed that 41 of these strains carried both the blaOXA-51-like and blaOXA-23-like genes. The presence rate of OXA-type β-lactamase genes and efflux pump genes in randomly selected positive strains is 100%. Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) annotation results indicated that the genes of these randomly selected positive strains were primarily involved in cellular processes, metabolic pathways, and environmental information processing, and exhibited strong enzymatic activity and binding functions. Length of hospital stay, ICU admission, prior carbapenem use, and mechanical ventilation are susceptibility factors for carbapenem resistance in A. baumannii infections at this hospital. MLST typing and multiplex PCR analysis indicate the spread of ST2-type blaOXA-51-like and blaOXA-23-like positive CRAB infections in the hospital, with ST2-type CRAB potentially being the dominant clone in circulation. Whole-genome sequencing revealed the resistance and virulence characteristics of CRAB strains isolated from clinical samples at this hospital, and showed that these CRAB strains from the hospital are distinct from those found in different provinces and cities in China.

title: Simpler is not always better: Phylodynamic misspecification and deep-learning corrections.
abstract: Phylodynamics bridges the gap between epidemiology and pathogen genetic data. The birth-death (BD) model and its extensions serve to infer the average number of secondary infections Re and the infection duration d from time-scaled pathogen phylogenies. Moreover, more complex models add extra parameters, such as the average length of the incubation period, the proportion of superspreaders in the infected population, or the speed-up in detection after contact-tracing. However, these additional parameters come at an important computational cost: While the simplest, BD, model, has a closed-form solution, its extensions do not and require numerical methods for their likelihood computation. This leads to increased computational times and potential numerical errors. Therefore, the BD model remains the favorite researchers'choice for real dataset analyses, and is often applied even in cases where more complex epidemiological aspects are present. We investigated, using simulations, how model misspecification influences inference of Re and d in the phylodynamic framework. We showed that the use of models not accounting for various epidemiological aspects leads to bias. In particular the simplest, BD, estimator tends to underestimate Re in the presence of super-spreading, incubation or contact-tracing, which might be dangerous from the public health perspective. In contrast, deep-learning-based estimators for complex models, accounting for multiple epidemiological factors, performed well in our simulations both on the data where those factors were present and where they were absent. This motivates the use of complex epidemiologically realistic estimators, whose design has recently become possible thanks to deep learning.

title: The evolution of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in Greek intensive care units is driven by local carbapenemase acquisition, nationwide nosocomial spread and emerging resistance to novel antimicrobials.
abstract: We investigated transmission patterns and therapeutic options for Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CR-Kp) in Greek ICUs. CR-Kp isolates (N=271) were prospectively collected from patients in 17 Greek ICUs between 2021-2023 (INCREASE study, funded by Pfizer). Susceptibility profiles were determined by broth microdilution and genomes sequenced with Oxford Nanopore. All isolates produced carbapenemases: 48% KPC, 20% NDM, 4.4% VIM, 27.6% multi-carbapenemase producers. Resistance to carbapenems, fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, and co-trimoxazole exceeded 90%, except for amikacin (73.4%) and colistin (46.5%). Aztreonam-avibactam and cefepime-zidebactam showed the highest susceptibility, 94.5% and 91.6% respectively, yet resistance was >10% among multi-carbapenemase producers. High levels of resistance to cefiderocol (41.7%) and cefepime-taniborbactam (21.4%) were detected. Aztreonam-avibactam resistance co-occurred with VEB-25 and a novel VEB variant. Predominant sequence types included ST39 (28.1%), ST11 (22.7%), and ST258 (18.4%). Time-scaled phylogenies demonstrated that following CG importation CR-Kp often acquired multiple carbapenemases. Over 88% of isolates were implicated in transmission clusters involving 1-8 ICUs across the country. In Greek ICUs, CR-Kp appears to emerge via local plasmid acquisition and then spread within and between hospitals. While aztreonam-avibactam and cefepime-zidebactam remain promising treatment options, resistance among multi-carbapenemase producers and diagnostic gaps (notably for VEB variants) are concerning.

title: Broad vaccine protection against globally diverse influenza A/H5Nx viruses.
abstract: Influenza A/H5Nx viruses continue to diversify and undergo gene reassortment as they infect avian and mammalian hosts worldwide. The severity of human infections varies substantially between different H5 clades and neuraminidase (NA) reassortants, creating unpredictable pandemic risk. Existing H5 vaccines, typically based on a single hemagglutinin (HA) strain, cannot keep pace with this natural variation. To address this problem, we computationally engineer HA, NA, and M2 antigens representing the global antigenic space of circulating H5Nx viruses, prioritizing N1 and N6 subtypes associated with the highest threat in humans. The resulting digitally immune-optimized mRNA vaccine, DVX-panH5Nx, elicits broad HA neutralization and NA inhibition across divergent clades in mice and ferrets. Compared to WHO candidate vaccine viruses (CVVs), DVX-panH5Nx confers superior protection against antigenically distinct H5N1 challenges spanning two decades of viral evolution, demonstrating that computationally designed multivalent antigen vaccines can overcome natural influenza diversification and provide a scalable strategy for pre-pandemic preparedness.
